title: What Makes a Question Curious? Measuring Model Curiosity in Human-LLM Interactions
abstract: arXiv:2610.33950v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Large language models increasingly act as partners in everyday communication. In these interactions, useful assistance may require not only answering, but also asking the right questions that surface knowledge gaps, assumptions, and alternatives. In this study, we refer to such epistemic question-asking as model curiosity, and introduce a theory-grounded taxonomy that distinguishes curiosity-oriented questions from generic model questioning. Across four conversation datasets, we find that curiosity-oriented questions remain rare (17-28% of all questions), but are associated with more exploratory and epistemically rich subsequent user responses, with varying patterns across datasets. We further conduct a human study to evaluate the usefulness of model curiosity, finding that curiosity can encourage exploration, especially in advice, creative, and research contexts. translated_title: 什么让问题充满好奇？测量人机交互中的模型好奇心
translated_abstract: 大型语言模型在日常交流中日益扮演着合作伙伴的角色。在这些互动中，有效的协助可能不仅需要回答问题，还需要提出恰当的问题，以揭示知识空白、假设和替代方案。在本研究中，我们将这类基于认知的问题提出行为称为“模型好奇心”，并引入了一个基于理论的分类体系，用以区分好奇心导向的问题与一般性的模型提问。通过对四个对话数据集的分析，我们发现好奇心导向的问题仍然较为罕见（占所有问题的17-28%），但其与用户后续更具探索性、认知上更丰富的回应相关联，且在不同数据集中呈现出不同的模式。我们进一步开展了一项人类研究来评估模型好奇心的有用性，发现好奇心能够鼓励探索，尤其是在建议、创意和研究场景中。这些发现对于构建更善于选择性提问的大型语言模型具有重要意义。
tldr: 该研究提出“模型好奇心”的概念及分类体系，发现好奇心导向的问题虽仅占17-28%且较为罕见，但能促使用户做出更具探索性和认知丰富性的回应，尤其在建议、创意和研究场景中能激发探索。
en_tdlr: This study introduces the concept and theory-grounded taxonomy of "model curiosity," finding that curiosity-oriented questions, though rare (17-28%), are associated with more exploratory and epistemically rich user responses, especially encouraging exploration in advice, creative, and research contexts.
